# DISCOVER - Veriry %File% Age to Confirm Data Transfer? 

 By JRA September 7, 2016 in MIS Systems 

### JRA 

 Posted September 7, 2016 

### JRA 

 Posted September 7, 2016 

Hi all - just having a bit of a think. A while back something broke that meant Discover didn't do it's data transfer overnight and we didn't notice for a while.

 Fixed now, but I was wondering if there was an easy way (say, reference the age of a file) to check as a scheduled task to verify this'd happened daily.

 Anyone got any ideas on that? Grateful for any help or suggestions.

 

### Greg 

You could write and schedule a script to search Discover.Warehouse.Service.log for problem key words, e.g the word "ERROR", and then return the line containing the key word and if the date = time of test then you know that something is wrong.

## We won and we didn't notice (The H)

 Posted Sep 5, 2011 18:17 UTC (Mon) by endecotp (guest, #36428) In reply to: We won and we didn't notice (The H) by cmccabe Parent article: We won and we didn't notice (The H)

> What you should do is run an application that does inotify on the > NFS server itself, monitoring the local filesystem that backs the > NFS-exported one 

 That's almost what I did; I learnt how to do multicast networking, and made each writing client announce when they made changes. (It didn't need to be perfectly reliable.) I was trying to make this work with an unmodifed server e.g. a home NAS box. 

 At that point I discovered the other thing that I alluded to before: if the writing client has appended a few bytes to the end of a large file, the reading client knows only that the file has changed and invalidates its entire cached copy. As you can guess, I didn't realise what was going on at first; once the file was a few tens of megabytes and it got slow I had a bang-head-on-keyboard moment. That project has now been on hold for a couple of years.
